# 7407 - Hex buffer/driver with open-collector high-voltage output

Package DIP-14 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7407.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7407.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 6 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7407 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7407.png) | ![7407 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/buf-ochv1.png) | ![7407 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/buf-ochv1.png) |

One rectangle split down the middle: left half empty, right half holds one diagonal from its bottom left corner to the middle of the right edge. High-voltage open collector: works like a plain open collector (it can only pull the line low; a pull-up resistor makes the 1, and several outputs may share one line), but the output transistor stands a higher voltage and a larger current. Per the TI datasheets: 7406/7407 up to 30 V, 7416/7417 up to 15 V, and up to 40 mA pulled low; a plain open collector such as 7405 stands only 5.5 V and 16 mA, so its pull-up must go to +5 V. High-voltage parts can switch a lamp, a relay or a 12 V line directly. The logic is the same. In the modern drawing it is marked HV beside the open-collector mark; that label is ours, not a standard symbol.

How to tell it on a drawing: Same split box as the open-collector AND (7409), but one input.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1Y = 1A | 1Y follows 1A (open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up). |
| 4 | 2Y = 2A | 2Y follows 2A (open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up). |
| 6 | 3Y = 3A | 3Y follows 3A (open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up). |
| 8 | 4Y = 4A | 4Y follows 4A (open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up). |
| 10 | 5Y = 5A | 5Y follows 5A (open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up). |
| 12 | 6Y = 6A | 6Y follows 6A (open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up). |

## Electrical

| Value | Figure |
|---|---|
| outputLowMaxCurrentMa | 40 |
| outputMaxVoltageV | 30 |
| inputSchmitt | no |
| notes | Non-inverting buffer/driver: IOL 40 mA vs 16 mA for a standard gate (7404), so it sinks two and a half times as much; the output may be pulled up to 30 V (7417: 15 V). Off-state leakage max 0.25 mA. |

| any | Y | PHL | 20 | 30 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 110 ohm, CL 15 pF |
| any | Y | PLH |  | 15 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 150 ohm, CL 50 pF |
| any | Y | PHL |  | 26 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 150 ohm, CL 50 pF |

## Notes

The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delay; minNs is null (the path-delay function uses 0 ns). No setup/hold/pulse-width limits apply to a gate, so timingLimits is empty.
